ranking.note: Raised to P1: release-branch integrity fix (Windows code signing verification) for an rc — the strongest release-integrity concern on the list after #36293.
Raised to P1: supported-platform build regression on macOS, milestoned 32.0 and tagged for backport, which the bands list as typical P1.
Raised to P2 and moved up: it is the prerequisite for #25573 and #36193, so it cannot sit below the P2 work it unblocks.
Raised to P2: removes a long-standing recurring burden (Boost.Test workarounds in depends/Guix, platform bugs), comparable in consequence to #28690.
Kept P2 on problem importance (project-wide standard transition) but placed after the concrete baseline bump #36042 it depends on.
Moved up: same RISC-V reproducible-build problem as P2 #35855, with independently reproduced hashes, so it belongs at the top of P3 rather than mid-list.
Moved up: measured 7-15 minute CI savings across ASan/MSan/Windows jobs is a concrete, verified gain ahead of other P3 conveniences.
Moved up: masked compiler errors make a CI job silently misleading, which this category ranks above general build friction.
Moved up: hidden Qt test output on Windows CI hides real failures, same class of problem as #36235.
Moved down: Windows IPC support matters for the multiprocess project but the affected binaries are experimental, unlike the release/CI issues above it.
Moved up to sit next to the other compiler-baseline bumps (#36042, #36287) it is sequenced with.
Moved up: same toolchain-baseline transition as #36036, which it overlaps with; they should be looked at together.
Moved down: useful contributor-friction tooling, which this category ranks below release integrity, platform breakage and CI-signal fixes.
Moved down: packager convenience with no effect on build integrity, platform support or CI signal.
Moved up: makes macOS Guix builds fail on linker warnings like other platforms, which is closer to release-build consistency than pure cosmetics.
Moved up: verified reproducible Guix output change to release binary size, stacked on #36272, so better reviewed with that stack.
Moved down: the size win is modest and the current patch has an identified correctness problem awaiting author changes.
Moved down: only affects builds against an external libmultiprocess, a narrow slice of developers.
Moved up to sit with #36167, from which it was split out.
Moved down: a new option on the experimental multiprocess path that depends on unmerged branches; value is real but contingent on work not yet in tree.
Moved down: warning-flag hygiene, grouped with the other warning-enabling PRs rather than ahead of platform and CI fixes.
Lowered to P4: maintainers have chosen to drop MSVC in favour of clang-cl (#31507), making this MSVC-only speedup largely redundant.
Lowered to P4: author confirms no CI failures have actually been observed from the current downloads, so the justification is weak and an alternative approach was suggested.

inconsistencies: #35855 and #36233 both update the Guix time-machine pin to fix native RISC-V builds (#36232); they overlap substantially. Review #35855 first as the broader toolchain update; if it lands, #36233 is largely redundant (or should be reduced to its riscv64 test overrides).
#24773 (HW SHA256 for MSVC) and #31507 (drop MSVC, use clang-cl) point in opposite directions on the same question. #31507 should be reviewed/decided first; #24773 is moot if MSVC support is dropped.
Chain: #36272 (split Guix Linux toolchain) is the stated prerequisite for both #25573 (static-pie) and #36193 (disable wchar_t libstdc++). Review order must be #36272 → #25573 / #36193.
Chain: #36042 (g++ 13) precedes #36033 (require C++23), which explicitly builds on the raised baseline; #36033 should not be reviewed as a standalone decision before #36042.

Overlap: #36036 bumps both Clang to 19 and Xcode CLT to 26.3, while #36287 bumps only Xcode CLT to 26.3. One is a subset of the other; decide which carries the macOS baseline bump to avoid conflicting changes to the same docs/CI.

#36275 (-Wunused-const-variable) was split out of #36167 (-Wunused); both also depend on upstream subtree merges (LevelDB/Minisketch/CRC32C/libmultiprocess). Review #36275 first as the narrower, landable piece.
#36267 consists of backports of already-merged master PRs (#36256, #36260); it is not duplicate work but its content should not be re-litigated, only verified for the 32.x branch.

#35068 and #35765 both fix depends-system correctness around native_libmultiprocess (host-package leakage vs stale local-source archives); they touch adjacent depends machinery and are best reviewed together.

#36268, #36275, #36167 and #35911 all enable additional compiler warning flags with mechanical tree-wide fixups; landing them in an arbitrary order will cause repeated conflicts across the same 60-170 files.
result.notes: The band split follows the category's own ordering: release integrity (#36293, #36267) and supported-platform build breakage (#36285) form P1; toolchain/reproducibility and release-like CI coverage form P2; individual build bugs, CI signal fixes and baseline bumps form a large P3; and cosmetic flags, logging and obsolete-flag removals form P4. The P3 band is unavoidably wide (34 PRs) because most of this category is per-PR build friction of similar weight; within it I ordered release-binary and depends correctness first, then CI-signal fixes, then developer convenience.
